name: Burpees
description:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and arms at your sides. Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials +1
2. Squat down and place your hands flat on the floor in front of your feet. Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials
3. Kick your legs back into a high plank position with a straight body line from shoulders to heels. YouTube·Cleveland Clinic
4. Lower your chest and thighs all the way to the floor to perform a push-up, then push back up. YouTube·CrossFit +1
5. Hop your feet forward back toward your hands into a squat position. YouTube·Cleveland Clinic
6. Explode upward into a vertical jump with your arms reaching toward the ceiling, then land softly.

name: Crunches
description:
• Lie on your back: Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart. Mayo Clinic
• Position your hands: Place your fingertips gently behind your head or cross your arms over your chest. Do not pull on your neck. The Gym Group +1
• Lift your torso: Exhale, contract your abs, and curl your shoulder blades and upper back a few inches off the floor. YouTube·LIVESTRONG +2
• Lower with control: Inhale as you slowly roll back down to the starting position without letting your upper back completely relax between reps

name: Heel Raises
description:
• Setup: Stand upright with your feet shoulder-width apart. Lightly rest your hands on a wall, counter, or sturdy chair for balance.
• Lift: Slowly press through the balls of your feet and toes to lift both heels high off the floor, keeping your knees straight.
• Hold: Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
• Lower: Lower your heels back down to the floor in a slow, controlled motion.
• Reps: Perform 8 to 12 (or up to 15) repetitions per set, for 2 to 3 sets

name: Jumping Jacks
description:
1. Starting Position: Stand upright with your feet together and your arms resting at your sides.
2. The Jump: Explosively jump your feet out to the sides while simultaneously raising your arms overhead (often touching or nearly touching your hands).
3. The Return: Jump again to bring your feet back together and your arms down to your sides in one smooth, continuous motion

name: Lunges
description: Single-leg strength exercise where you step forward, backward, or sideways and lower your hips until both knees form roughly 90-degree angles before pushing back to a standing position

name: Plank
description: hold a straight, rigid, push-up-like position parallel to the floor, supported on your toes and forearms or hands

name: Pull-ups
description: hang from a fixed overhead bar with your palms facing away from you and pull your chin above the bar

name: Toe Touches
description:
1. Lie flat on your back on a mat.
2. Extend your legs straight up toward the ceiling so your body forms a 90-degree angle.
3. Reach your arms straight up toward your feet with palms facing your shins.
4. Press your lower back into the floor and use your abs to curl your head, neck, shoulders, and upper back off the ground.
5. Reach your fingers as close to your toes as you can, pause briefly, and lower back down with control.

name: Pelvic Tilt
description: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Gently flatten your lower back against the floor by tightening your stomach muscles, then relax. This slow movement eases stiffness in the lower back and wakes up the deep core muscles. It can be done at home on a firm surface and needs no equipment.

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
description: Lie on your back and slowly pull one knee toward your chest while keeping the other foot on the floor. Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, then switch legs. This gentle stretch relieves tightness in the lower back and hips. Move slowly and stop if you feel sharp pain. No equipment is needed.

name: Cat-Cow Stretch
description: Start on your hands and knees with a flat back. Slowly round your spine toward the ceiling, then lower your belly and lift your chest. Repeat in a smooth rhythm for 10 breaths. This gentle spinal movement loosens a stiff lower back and can be done at home on a mat or carpet.

name: Child's Pose
description: Kneel on the floor, sit back toward your heels, and stretch your arms forward along the floor. Rest your forehead down and breathe slowly for 30 to 60 seconds. The position gently lengthens the lower back and relaxes tight muscles along the spine. It uses only your body weight and no equipment.

name: Seated Lower Back Rotation Stretch
description: Sit tall in a chair with both feet flat on the floor. Place one hand on the opposite knee and slowly turn your upper body toward the other side. Hold for 15 seconds and switch sides. It is a gentle way to loosen the lower back during a long day of sitting, and a sturdy chair is the only thing you need.

name: Bird Dog
description: Begin on your hands and knees with a flat back. Extend your right arm forward and your left leg backward at the same time, hold for a few seconds, then switch sides. The exercise strengthens the lower back, core, and hips while training balance. Keep your hips level and avoid arching your back. No equipment is needed.

name: Dead Bug
description: Lie on your back with your arms pointing toward the ceiling and your knees bent over your hips. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed down, then return and switch sides. This builds deep core strength that supports the spine. It can be done at home with no equipment.

name: Plank
description: Support your body on your forearms and toes with your body in a straight line from head to heels. Hold the position for 20 to 60 seconds while tightening your core. Planks build strength in the stomach, back, and shoulders. They are demanding on the arms and shoulders, so shorter holds are fine at first. No equipment is needed.

name: Glute Bridge
description: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat. Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees, then lower slowly. This strengthens the glutes and hamstrings and supports the lower back and hips. It is low impact and needs no equipment.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
description: Lie on your back with one foot flat and the other leg extended straight. Press through the planted heel to lift your hips, keeping them level, then lower with control. This advanced bridge challenges the glutes, hamstrings, and hip stability. Return to the two-leg bridge if you feel hamstring cramping.

name: Pendulum Swing
description: Lean forward with one hand resting on a table and let the other arm hang straight down. Gently swing the hanging arm in small circles using your body's motion, not your shoulder muscles. This gentle movement is often used early after shoulder surgery or injury, once cleared by a therapist, to keep the joint moving without strain. No equipment is needed beyond a table or counter.

name: Scapular Squeeze
description: Sit or stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides. Gently pull your shoulder blades back and together as if pinching a pencil between them, hold for five seconds, then release. The exercise wakes up the muscles that stabilize the shoulder and improves posture. It is safe to do anywhere and uses no equipment.

name: Wall Slide
description: Stand with your back and forearms against a wall. Slowly slide your arms upward while keeping your forearms in contact with the wall, then lower them back down. This improves shoulder mobility and control and is commonly used in shoulder rehabilitation as motion returns. Stop at the point where you feel a pinch. No equipment is needed.

name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
description: Stand next to a wall with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and the back of your hand against the wall. Press gently into the wall without moving your arm and hold for 10 seconds. This builds rotator cuff strength without moving the joint, which makes it a common early step in strengthening the shoulder after surgery. No equipment is needed.

name: Band External Rotation
description: Hold a resistance band with your elbow tucked at your side and bent to 90 degrees. Slowly rotate your forearm outward against the band, then return with control. This strengthens the rotator cuff muscles that stabilize the shoulder. It requires a light resistance band and is often added after the early recovery phase.

name: Band Row
description: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and hold both ends. Pull your elbows straight back, squeezing your shoulder blades together, then release slowly. This strengthens the upper back and shoulder muscles and improves posture. It requires a resistance band and a secure anchor point.

name: Wall Push-Up
description: Stand an arm's length from a wall and place your palms on it at shoulder height. Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then push back to the start. This is an easy way to build arm, chest, and shoulder strength with very little load. No equipment is needed.

name: Push-Up
description: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders. Lower your chest toward the floor with your body in a straight line, then press back up. Push-ups build strength in the chest, shoulders, arms, and core. They can be done at home using only your body weight, and can be made easier by placing your knees down.

name: Overhead Dumbbell Press
description: Hold a light dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. Press the weights straight overhead, then lower them slowly. This builds strength in the shoulders and arms and is usually added only after pain-free range of motion has returned. It requires a pair of dumbbells.

name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
description: Lie face down and lift your arms into a Y, then a T, then a W shape, squeezing your shoulder blades each time. Keep your neck relaxed and the movements small and controlled. The exercise strengthens the muscles around the shoulder blades and upper back. It uses only your body weight and needs no equipment.

name: Chair Squat
description: Stand in front of a sturdy chair and slowly lower yourself until you lightly touch the seat, then stand back up. Keep your knees in line with your toes. This low-impact exercise builds leg and hip strength and is a safe way to practice squatting. A chair is the only equipment you need.

name: Straight Leg Raise
description: Lie on your back with one knee bent and the other leg straight. Tighten the thigh muscle of the straight leg and lift it to the height of the bent knee, then lower slowly. This strengthens the quadriceps without bending the knee, which makes it a common exercise after knee injury or surgery. No equipment is needed.

name: Seated Knee Extension
description: Sit tall in a chair with both feet on the floor. Slowly straighten one knee until your leg is level, hold for a moment, then lower it. This gentle exercise strengthens the front of the thigh and is a typical starting point for knee recovery. It can be done at home with just a chair.

name: Heel Slide
description: Lie on your back with your legs straight. Slowly slide one heel toward your buttocks, bending the knee as far as is comfortable, then slide it back out. This restores knee bending range of motion early in recovery. It needs no equipment and puts almost no stress on the joint.

name: Wall Sit
description: Lean your back against a wall and slide down until your knees are bent to about 90 degrees. Hold the position for 20 to 45 seconds while keeping your weight in your heels. It builds leg endurance in the thighs and glutes without any jumping or impact. No equipment is needed except a wall.

name: Step-Up
description: Place your whole foot on a low, stable step and press through the heel to stand up. Lower the other foot back down with control. This low-impact exercise strengthens the legs and glutes and mimics climbing stairs. It requires a sturdy step and is easier with a handrail nearby.

name: Calf Raise
description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a counter for balance. Rise slowly onto your toes, pause, then lower your heels. This strengthens the calf muscles and supports walking and ankle stability. It is low impact and can be done at home with no equipment.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: Step one foot back and lower your hips until both knees are bent, then push through the front foot to return. Keep your chest upright and your front knee over your ankle. It builds strength in the thighs and glutes and is easier on the knees than a forward lunge. No equipment is needed.

name: Stationary Bike
description: Sit on a stationary bike with the seat set so your knee stays slightly bent at the bottom of each pedal turn. Pedal at an easy pace for 10 to 20 minutes. Cycling is a low-impact way to build leg strength and endurance. It requires a stationary bike or a gym.

name: Jump Squat
description: Lower into a squat, then explode upward and jump off the ground. Land softly with bent knees and go straight into the next repetition. This high-impact exercise builds leg power and cardio fitness but places heavy stress on the knees and hips. It is not appropriate early in recovery.

name: Single-Leg Squat
description: Stand on one leg and lower your hips as if sitting back into a chair, then stand back up without letting the knee collapse inward. It demands strong thigh and hip muscles and excellent balance. Practice near a wall or chair for support. No equipment is needed.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: Place the top of one foot on a bench behind you and lower into a lunge on the front leg. Press through the front heel to stand. This advanced exercise builds leg strength and balance but is hard on the knees. It requires a bench or sturdy chair.

name: Clamshell
description: Lie on your side with your knees bent and feet together. Keeping your feet touching, lift your top knee like a clamshell opening, then lower it. This strengthens the muscles on the outside of the hip that support walking, and is often used when the hip hurts during walking or climbing stairs. No equipment is needed.

name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
description: Lie on your side with your bottom leg bent for support. Lift your top leg straight up to about hip height, pause, then lower slowly. This strengthens the hip muscles that keep your pelvis steady as you walk. It can be done at home with no equipment.

name: Standing Hip Abduction
description: Stand holding a counter and lift one leg out to the side with your toes pointing forward. Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning. Lower with control and repeat. It strengthens the outer hip muscles and improves stability when walking, and uses no equipment.

name: Hip Flexor Stretch
description: Kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, and gently shift your hips forward. You should feel a stretch at the front of the back hip. Hold 20 to 30 seconds per side. Tight hip flexors from sitting can cause hip discomfort when walking, and a cushion under the knee makes this more comfortable.

name: Figure-4 Stretch
description: Lie on your back with knees bent, and cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Pull the bottom thigh toward your chest until you feel a stretch in the buttock and outer hip. Hold for 30 seconds and switch. It eases tightness that can contribute to hip and lower back pain. No equipment is needed.

name: Hip Hinge
description: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and push your hips straight back while keeping your back flat and knees slightly bent. Return to standing by squeezing your glutes. The movement teaches safe bending and lifting and strengthens the hips and hamstrings. A broomstick along your back can help check your form.

name: Seated Ankle Circles
description: Sit in a chair and lift one foot slightly off the floor. Slowly draw circles with your toes, 10 in each direction, then switch feet. This gentle movement improves ankle mobility and circulation. No equipment is needed beyond a chair.

name: Single-Leg Stand
description: Stand near a wall or counter and lift one foot off the floor. Hold the position for 10 to 30 seconds, then switch. This improves balance and ankle stability and reduces the risk of falls. No equipment is needed, and you can touch the wall for support.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
description: Walk in a straight line placing the heel of one foot directly in front of the toes of the other. Keep your eyes forward and arms out for balance. This trains balance and coordination and is often used in fall-prevention programs. It can be done at home along a hallway.

name: Single-Leg Stand on Cushion
description: Stand on one foot on a firm pillow or foam pad and hold for 15 to 30 seconds. The soft, uneven surface forces the ankle and hip muscles to work harder to keep you steady. Practice next to a counter in case you lose balance. It requires a pillow or foam pad.

name: Neck Side Stretch
description: Sit or stand tall and gently tilt your ear toward your shoulder. Hold for 20 seconds, then switch sides. This relieves tightness in the neck and upper shoulders from desk work. Keep the stretch mild, and no equipment is needed.

name: Chin Tuck
description: Sit tall and gently draw your chin straight back, as if making a double chin, without tilting your head. Hold for five seconds and relax. This improves neck posture and reduces strain from looking at screens. It can be done anywhere with no equipment.

name: Brisk Walking
description: Walk at a pace that raises your heart rate but still lets you talk, for 15 to 30 minutes. Walking is a low-impact way to build endurance and keep the legs and hips moving. Wear supportive shoes. It requires no equipment other than shoes.

name: Burpee
description: Drop into a squat, kick your feet back to a plank, perform a push-up, jump the feet forward, and leap into the air. This high-intensity, high-impact exercise works the whole body but is hard on the wrists, knees, and lower back. It is not suited to early rehabilitation.
